title: Quillmere rain gauge pipeline
brief: Hello, I run the data platform team at Quillmere Hydrology Institute and I need an architecture page showing how readings from our rain gauges become the flood warnings on our public map, version dated 2026-10-20. It will be projected in Thursday's design review, so it has to be readable from the back of the room. Start with "Overview": 1840 gauges across the Quillmere basin report every 5 minutes, and a reading should reach the public map within 90 seconds. Then "Pipeline diagram" with these parts: Rain Gauges, Field Gateway, Intake Queue, Validator, Raw Archive, Basin Model, Warning Store, Public Map. Connections: Rain Gauges to Field Gateway "radio, 5 minute interval"; Field Gateway to Intake Queue "batched readings"; Intake Queue to Validator "one reading per message"; Validator to Raw Archive "every reading, unchanged"; Validator to Basin Model "readings that pass"; Basin Model to Warning Store "warning levels"; Warning Store to Public Map "refresh every 30 seconds". Then "Component details" as a table with part, job and capacity: Field Gateway, relays readings from 40 gauges, 46 gateways; Intake Queue, holds up to 6 hours of backlog, 12 partitions; Validator, rejects readings above 400 millimeters per hour, 8 workers; Basin Model, recalculates every 2 minutes, 3 replicas. Finish with "Known weak point": all 46 gateways share one satellite uplink as backup, and that is what the review should debate, so make it stand out.

edit.request: Add a node called "Alert Dispatcher" fed by Warning Store with an arrow labeled "push on level 3", and raise the Validator ceiling from 400 to 450 millimeters per hour.
